jobs.occupation: Social Media Lead
jobs.description:
Samsøe Samsøe is looking for a Social Media Lead to shape and drive our global social media presence.

We are looking for a self-driven and experienced profile with a strong understanding of social media, fashion and culture, combined with a great eye for content. You know what makes an image or video work, understand how different platforms behave and can turn ideas into relevant, engaging content.

This is a role with a high level of ownership, combining strategic direction with hands-on content creation. You will work closely with Brand, Creative, Marketing, and E-commerce to ensure Samsøe Samsøe shows up on social in a way that feels distinctive, relevant and true to the brand.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• 
Own and continuously develop the global social media strategy for Samsøe Samsøe.

• 
Lead the planning and execution of the social content calendar across Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest and emerging platforms.

• 
Translate collections, campaigns and brand stories into strong, platform-native social concepts and content.

• 
Create social-first photo and video content independently when relevant, from ideation and shooting through to editing and publishing.

• 
Bring a strong visual perspective to our channels, with a solid understanding of photography, videography, composition, lighting, movement and editing.

• 
Identify opportunities for agile and low-production content alongside larger campaign and brand productions.

• 
Work closely with Creative and Brand teams to develop content while maintaining a strong and consistent visual identity and tone of voice.

• 
Identify cultural moments, conversations, trends and emerging formats relevant to the Samsøe Samsøe universe – and know which ones are right for the brand.

• 
Develop strategies for community growth and engagement, building a relevant and engaged global audience.

• 
Partner with E-commerce and Performance Marketing to support commercial priorities while protecting and strengthening the brand.

• 
Manage content publishing, channel optimisation and ongoing platform development.

• 
Use data and audience insights to understand performance, identify opportunities and continuously improve our approach.

• 
Define and report on relevant social KPIs, translating performance into clear recommendations and actions.

• 
Stay ahead of developments in social media, fashion, culture and digital behaviour and proactively bring new ideas into the organisation.

• 
Manage relevant external partners, creators and agencies when needed.

YOUR PROFILE

You bring a strong combination of social media expertise, creative judgement and hands-on content skills. You understand fashion and visual culture and have a clear sense of what makes content relevant to both a brand and its audience.

You are self-driven and comfortable taking ownership. You spot opportunities, develop ideas and make things happen without needing constant direction. You have the maturity and judgement to make decisions independently while working collaboratively across teams.

We imagine that you:

• 
Have 4+ years of relevant experience in social media and content creation, ideally within fashion, lifestyle or another culturally relevant industry.

• 
Have a strong visual eye and practical photography, videography and editing skills.

• 
Understand social-first storytelling and how to create content specifically for different platforms.

• 
Have a deep understanding of Instagram, TikTok and the wider social landscape.

• 
Combine strategic thinking with the ability and willingness to create and execute yourself.

• 
Have a strong understanding of fashion, brands, culture and emerging creative formats.

• 
Are proactive, resourceful and confident taking an idea from concept to execution.

• 
Are comfortable using data and insights to inform creative and strategic decisions.

• 
Can manage multiple priorities and stakeholders in a fast-moving environment.

• 
Have excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

As our workforce is increasingly more international, our corporate language is English. If you can identify with our concept and our ambitions, we look forward to receiving your application.

We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment and encourage everyone to apply for the position, regardless of age, national and cultural background, gender identity, religion, sexual orientation, or disability.

jobs.occupation: Senior Authorised Person (SAP) – Switching Leader
jobs.description:
Senior Authorised Person (SAP) – Electrical Operations / Switching Leader

Location: DenmarkEmployment type: Full-timeEmployer: Global Nordics 

Job Description

We are seeking an experienced Senior Authorised Person (SAP) / Switching Leader (Koblingsleder) to support electrical operations on a major engineering project in Denmark.

The successful candidate will be responsible for coordinating safe switching operations, electrical isolations and safety procedures across high-voltage (HV) and low-voltage (LV) electrical systems.

The position operates within an established electrical safety management structure, under the designated Operation Manager (Driftsansvarlig Person), and in accordance with applicable Danish electrical safety regulations and EN 50110-1.

Key Responsibilities

• 
Plan, coordinate and oversee HV and LV switching operations.

• 
Prepare and review switching schedules and electrical safety documentation.

• 
Coordinate electrical isolations, earthing and safe access procedures.

• 
Prepare, issue and cancel safety documents within the scope of assigned authorisation.

• 
Coordinate with Control Engineers and electrical work teams during operational activities.

• 
Ensure appropriate safety precautions are implemented before electrical work begins.

• 
Supervise and coordinate personnel involved in electrical operational activities.

• 
Support commissioning, energisation and electrical system handover.

• 
Maintain accurate switching records, operational logs and safety documentation.

• 
Participate in safety audits, risk assessments and toolbox talks.

• 
Ensure compliance with site-specific electrical safety procedures and applicable Danish regulations.

Qualifications and Experience

• 
Relevant qualification in electrical engineering or equivalent professional experience.

• 
Extensive experience working with HV and LV electrical systems.

• 
Previous experience as a Senior Authorised Person, Switching Leader, Control Engineer or equivalent.

• 
Strong understanding of electrical switching, isolation, earthing and safe working procedures.

• 
Knowledge of EN 50110-1 and electrical safety management systems.

• 
Experience preparing switching schedules and electrical safety documentation.

• 
Demonstrated ability to coordinate electrical work teams and operational activities.

• 
Strong communication, organisational and safety leadership skills.

• 
Good command of English.

Electrical Safety Requirements

The successful candidate will undergo a competence assessment and receive the necessary written operational appointment and authorisation under the project's Danish electrical safety management arrangements (KLS-D) before undertaking regulated electrical activities.

The role does not include statutory Operation Manager responsibilities or electrical installation work requiring separate company authorisation.

Application

Please submit your CV, relevant qualifications and details of your professional experience.

jobs.occupation: Head of the Nordic-Baltic Cyber Consortium (NBCC)
jobs.description:
About the positionThe Danish Resilience Agency (SAMSIK) is seeking a highly experienced and strategic leader to serve as Head of the Nordic-Baltic Cyber Consortium (NBCC).The NBCC is a Danish-hosted, EU-supported cybersecurity initiative established under the EU Cyber Solidarity Act. The consortium brings together Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania and Norway to build and operate a regional cyber hub that strengthens situational awareness and analytical capacity across the Nordic-Baltic region.As Head of the NBCC, you will be responsible for establishing and leading a new international organisation of strategic importance to both regional and European cybersecurity. While formally employed by the Danish Resilience Agency, you will report to the NBCC Executive Board, composed of senior representatives from the participating national cybersecurity authorities, and operate in close coordination with EU institutions.The position is based in Copenhagen, Denmark.Key responsibilitiesStrategic leadership and governance

• 
Provide overall strategic direction and leadership of the NBCC in line with EU objectives, consortium agreements and national mandates.

• 
Develop, implement and continuously adjust the NBCC’s strategic roadmap, including the phased build-up from initial deployment to full operational capability.

• 
Ensure alignment between the NBCC activities, EU cybersecurity policies and the strategic interests of participating member states.

Management, organisation and budget

• 
Act as head of the NBCC organisation, including direct line management of up to eight permanent staff based in Denmark and professional oversight of national analysts located in each participating member state.

• 
Build and lead a cohesive multinational organisation with a shared operational culture, while managing differing national frameworks and practices.

• 
Ensure sound financial management, reporting and documentation in accordance with EU and national requirements.

Operational responsibility

• 
Hold overall responsibility for the NBCC’s operational delivery, including the secure and reliable operation of platforms for cyber threat intelligence sharing, analytical collaboration and communication.

• 
Ensure structured and timely sharing of relevant cyber threat information and contribution to regional and European situational awareness.

About youTo succeed in this role, we expect that you:

• 
Have proven experience leading multinational or international cooperation involving multiple stakeholders and governance layers; experience from Nordic-Baltic cooperation is a strong advantage.

• 
Possess a strong understanding of cyber threat intelligence, incident response ecosystems and information-sharing mechanisms at national and international level.

• 
Have demonstrated experience with EU cooperation, preferably including EU-funded projects and engagement with EU institutions.

• 
Are able to operate confidently at senior political and administrative levels, nationally and internationally.

• 
Can demonstrate strong regional insight and experience, for example from a Nordic or Baltic cybersecurity authority or a comparable organisation.

 In addition, you:

• 
Exercise strong strategic judgement and are able to balance political, operational and technical considerations.

• 
Have excellent leadership and communication skills and are able to build trust across national and organisational boundaries.

• 
Are fully proficient in English; knowledge of one or more Nordic or Baltic languages is an advantage. Danish language skills are not required.

About the Danish Resilience AgencyThe Danish Resilience Agency is under the authority of the Danish Ministry for Resilience and Preparedness. The agency is responsible for tasks related to cybersecurity, crisis management, physical security and protection of critical infrastructure.We advise and support authorities, companies and key societal functions in preventing and managing incidents and crises. The agency currently employs approximately 300 staff members working across disciplines in a highly engaged and mission-driven environment.About the NBCCThe NBCC is a Nordic-Baltic cybersecurity cooperation supported by the EU. Through the NBCC, the participating countries jointly establish and operate a regional cyber hub that enhances collective situational awareness and analytical capacity.The NBCC will jointly procure cybersecurity capabilities with the EU, employ analysts in Copenhagen and across the member states, and contribute to the European Cybersecurity Shield. The NBCC is organised as a distinct entity within the Danish Resilience Agency and is accountable to its Executive Board.As Head of the NBCC, you will be responsible for building this organisation from the ground up and for strengthening collective regional resilience against cyber threats.Salary and terms of employmentSalary and terms of employment will depend on qualifications and experience and will be determined in accordance with the collective agreements applicable to employees in the Danish state. The area of employment is the Danish Ministry for Resilience and Preparedness.Employment is conditional on obtaining and maintaining a Danish security clearance at SECRET (DK: HEMMELIGT) level for the duration of employment.The position is a fixed-term appointment for a period of 4 years, with the possibility of extension.The position is full-time 37-hours per week, and the duty station is Holsteinsgade 63, 2100 Copenhagen.To be eligible for employment EU/EEA Citizens are required to obtain an EU residence document as proof of your right to reside and work in Denmark. Non-EU/EEA Citizens must hold a valid residence and work permit before you can begin working in Denmark. Citizens of Sweden, Norway, Finland, or Iceland do not require a residence or work permit to live and work in Denmark. For more detailed information regarding the regulations for your specific citizenship, please visit: New to Denmark and/or Info Norden | Nordisk SamarbejdeIf the position is filled by an applicant not currently residing in Denmark, the Danish Resilience Agency is prepared to offer a relocation package of up to 45.000 DKK. Any other costs related to relocation or housing must be covered by the employee.Are you interested?Please submit your application via the “Apply” button on this page. Your application must be received by the recruitment system no later than 15th November 2026 and must include a CV and relevant diplomas of education.For further information about the position, please contact Kia Slæbæk Jensen at +45 2134 1851 or Morten Bro at +45 2178 4257.All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply regardless of personal background.Applications may be shared with participants from the employment committee from all participating countries.

jobs.occupation: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy
jobs.description:
Declaration of interest regarding PhD project:

The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy, with background in one or more of the following areas: philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, phenomenology.We are looking for a person with a relevant degree (M.A., MSc. etc.) in philosophy or a related field. Starting date is September 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is fully funded, full-time, for three years. The PhD degree will be awarded by the Faculty of Health Sciences.

 

Research environment

The PhD student will be based in the research group of Applied and Interdisciplinary Phenomenology in the Department of Psychology, SDU, at the Odense campus. The research group develops, disseminates, and applies methods to support cutting-edge research into subjectivity and the nature of human experience. Current group members have backgrounds in philosophy, psychology, anthropology, neuroscience, environmental studies, and pain research.

The group directly supports the professional development of its members, most of whom are postdocs or PhD students. In addition to receiving support from the project team, the PhD student will be supported by the broader group to develop their research, presentation, and teaching skills, as well as other academic skills, including those required for organizing academic activities such as workshops and conferences and for successful grant-writing. The PhD student will therefore be provided with the requisite knowledge and skills for pursuing an academic career in Europe or abroad.

The PhD student will also be provided with a work computer and a dedicated workspace at the Department of Psychology.

 

Project description

The PhD student will be part of the project, Understanding Experiences of Mood Disturbances in Depression (DEPMOOD), led by Anthony Vincent Fernandez. The project is funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark and runs for four years, starting September 1st, 2026. The PhD student will join the project for the final three years, collaborating with the PI, a psychology postdoc, and several external partners in Europe and the US, including philosophers, clinical psychologists, and psychiatrists.

The aim of the project is to establish a taxonomy of the variety of mood disturbances experienced by people diagnosed with depression, providing more precise characterizations of symptoms than those currently offered by concepts such as “depressed mood” or “anhedonia”. The project combines philosophical and qualitative methods, and includes in-depth interviews with people diagnosed with depression. The PhD student will not be expected to carry out interviews, as these will be conducted by the postdoc and external project partners. The PhD student’s primary role will be to help analyze the interview data using a combination of qualitative and philosophical methods. Their PhD thesis will therefore be a theoretical contribution, but will build upon the project’s empirical dataset.

In addition to producing a thesis, the PhD student will be required to take a variety of short PhD courses, carry out an international research stay, and fulfil light teaching duties.

The PhD student will be provided with DKK 10,000 per year for travel. Additional funds may be available.

 

Qualifications

Before the start date of September 1st, 2027, the applicant should have a master’s degree in philosophy or a related field and total course credits equivalent to 300 ECTS. Typically, this is a total of at least five years of education combined between bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with 60 ECTS obtained for every full year of study.

The candidate should have a background in philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, and/or phenomenology. Familiarity with qualitative research methods (especially analysis methods) is an advantage, but by no means required.

The candidate should be proficient in English. Proficiency in Danish or another Scandinavian language may be an advantage, but is not required.

For further information about the project, please contact:Anthony Vincent Fernandez

Department of Psychology

University of Southern Denmark (SDU)

E-mail: afernandez@health.sdu.dk

Please note that while we are happy to provide answers to questions about the position and application process, direct feedback on application materials cannot be provided.

Applications must include (in English, or with a certified English translation):

 

• 
A letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”.

• 
Detailed CV, including personal contact information as well as any publications or presentations

• 
Certified copy of diploma and transcripts (Master’s degree in a relevant field). If the applicant is in the process of completing their master’s degree, they should provide transcripts along with a letter from their supervisor confirming expected completion of their degree before September 1st, 2027.

• 
Writing sample of maximum 10,000 words (e.g., publication, conference paper, selection from a master’s thesis). If the sample exceeds this length, please indicate which section should be read.

• 
A document listing 2-3 references, with contact information and a brief note about your relation to the reference. Note that reference letters will only be requested for candidates invited to interview. 

At this stage, no project proposal is required. Candidates invited to interview will be asked to prepare a brief project plan.

Please do not use generative AI in the formulation of any application materials. The purpose of these materials is to gain a clear sense of you and your abilities.

Shortlisting and interviews may be used in the assessment process. 

For purposes of evaluation and assessment, application materials may be shared with external members of the project team at Aarhus University and Amsterdam University Medical Center.

Further information about the PhD-study can be found at the homepage of the University.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated

 

Closing date January 15th, 2027 

We expect to conduct interviews within two months of the application closing date.Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students. 

The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order)

 

Salary and Working Conditions at SDU

PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement.Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98   per year.

The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark is one of Denmark’s leading faculties of health sciences. With nine departments, internationally top‑class research, and a broad range of health‑related study programmes, we contribute to developing the knowledge, treatments, and healthcare system of the future.

As an employee at the faculty, you become part of an ambitious and interdisciplinary environment characterised by high academic standards, strong collaborations, and excellent opportunities for professional development. The faculty has activities in Odense, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. In Esbjerg and Copenhagen, strong academic communities provide the framework for research and education, while our modern faculty building in Odense brings research, education, and administration together under one roof and is directly connected to Odense University Hospital.The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor in Global Health at The Research Unit of General Practice, University of Southern Denmark
jobs.description:
The Research Unit of General Practice at the Institute of Public Health, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 2-year full time Assistant Professor position in Global Health. The position starts on April 1, 2027, and will terminate at the end of the appointment period unless otherwise agreed.

Beskrivelse til interne kandidater

The Research Unit of General Practice at the Institute of Public Health, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 2-year full time Assistant Professor position in Global Health.

The position starts on April 1, 2027, and will terminate at the end of the appointment period unless otherwise agreed.

Job DescriptionThe position involves research in global health with a particular focus on strengthening primary healthcare systems for vulnerable and underserved populations in low- and middle-income countries. The successful candidate will contribute to the international research project STRENGTHENing Gender-Responsive Health Systems for Addressing Non-Communicable Diseases in Climate-Affected Fishing Communities in Western Kenya (STRENGTHEN) and other upcoming global health projects. The STRENGTHEN project aims to improve the prevention and management of NCDs in climate-affected fishing communities in Western Kenya by making the health systems even more gender-responsive. The project will generate evidence on how community health promoters (CHPs) provide NCD care in FEDCs affected by climate change. It will address five key health systems building blocks: health information systems, health workforce, health service, medical technology, and policy and governance. The work will involve conducting implementation and health services research, and collaborating with researchers, healthcare professionals, policymakers, and community stakeholders across different country settings. The position involves travel to Kenya for short periods.

We offer a challenging position in a stimulating research environment with excellent opportunities for collaboration within SDU and with international research partners.

Expectations of qualificationsThe successful applicant should have:

• 
A PhD degree (or equivalent) in Global Health, Public Health, Epidemiology, Health Services Research, Implementation Science, or a related discipline

• 
A strong background in health systems research, primary healthcare, chronic disease prevention and management, or health equity research in low- and middle-income countries

• 
A strong academic record

• 
Good collaboration and communication skills

• 
Interest in co-supervising BSc, MSc and PhD students

Following qualifications are preferred:

• 
Experience with mixed-methods research, including qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis

• 
Experience with implementation science, intervention development, and evaluation of community-based health programmes

• 
Experience with global health research conducted in low- and middle-income countries and/or humanitarian settings

• 
Experience with stakeholder engagement and collaboration with healthcare providers, communities, and policymakers

• 
Experience with writing research applications

• 
Experience in teaching and education

Further informationFor further information please contact Prof. Jens Søndergaard, jsondergaard@health.sdu.dk, or Associate Prof. Trine Thilsing, tthilsing@health.sdu.dk 

Application deadline and interviewsThe application deadline is November15th 2026 at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST)  

Terms of employment Appointment as an assistant professor is temporary and for an initial 2-year period, and the preferred start date is from 1. April 2027.

During employment, the assistant professor will complete the Lecturer Training Programme, if this has not already been completed.   

Appointment as an assistant professor requires academic qualifications at PhD level. 

Further information on the appointment procedure can be found in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities. 

The appointment is in accordance with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations .

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation.  

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”. 

Application Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below.  

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.  

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.  

Your application must include the following as PDF files: 

Please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total). 

• 
a motivation letter.  

• 
a detailed CV.  

• 
degree certificates (including a Ph.D.-diploma). 

• 
a complete and numbered list of publications.  

• 
3 to 5 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please note that a copy of each publication must be attached as a pdf file.  

• 
It is permitted to merge copies of the selected publications into a single PDF file. 

• 
a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy.  

• 
a research plan an explanation of other qualifications relevant to the position. 

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application.

Applications received after the deadline and/or incomplete applications will not be considered. 

If you experience technical problems, you must contact hcm-support@sdu.dk.

Assessment and selection process Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. 

About UsThe Research Unit of General Practice is a collaboration between the Research Unit of General Practice in Odense-Esbjerg, which is organizationally affiliated with the Foundation for General Practice Research (FEA), and the Research Unit of General Practice at the Department of Public Health, University of Southern Denmark (SDU).

The primary objective of the Research Unit is to contribute to the improvement and development of health and healthcare for patients, with a particular focus on services provided in and around general practice. 

A cornerstone of our educational activities is the training of Master's and PhD students. In addition, we contribute to teaching across a range of health sciences bachelor's and master's degree programmes at the Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark, as well as within the Research Training Programme of the specialist training programme in general practice.

Further information about The Faculty of Health Sciences. 

Living and working in DenmarkForeign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. 

The International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. 

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: A position as postdoc (100% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. The position is limited to three years.
jobs.description:
A position as postdoc (100% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. The position is limited to three years. The starting date is 01 February 2027 or later by agreement and depending on the candidate’s preferences.

We are seeking a researcher with documented experience in epidemiological research who can independently plan studies, conduct analyses and write scientific papers. We are looking for a future colleague with a clear academic interest in women’s mental health and the motivation to develop their research in this field. Experience in psychiatric epidemiology is a distinct advantage.

The project

The position is funded by a grant from the Wellcome Trust through PROMIS, an international research project on women’s mental health during perimenopause. The project is in its initial phase and will draw on cohort data linked to national registers, in collaboration with researchers in the UK, the USA and Sweden.

The project investigates risk factors for the onset or recurrence of depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder and psychotic disorders during perimenopause. The work includes epidemiological studies of risk, the development and validation of prediction models, and studies of hormone therapy and mental health outcomes using target trial emulation.

Research tasks

The postdoc will work closely with Principal Investigator Professor Trine Munk-Olsen and the project’s data analyst and participate actively in the international research collaboration. The candidate will have considerable scope to shape research questions, the structure of individual studies, study designs and methodological choices within the framework of the project.

The main tasks are to:

• 
Plan and conduct epidemiological studies using register and cohort data, including preparing study protocols and analysis plans.

• 
Independently perform statistical analyses, interpret results and write scientific papers.

• 
Identify risk factors for mental disorders during perimenopause and contribute to the development and validation of prediction models.

• 
Contribute to studies using target trial emulation to investigate hormone therapy and mental health outcomes.

• 
Together with other project team members, contribute to applications for access to external datasets and to the maintenance, quality assurance, harmonisation and documentation of the datasets used.

• 
Participate in subprojects and undertake tasks within the international collaboration, including coordination, organising project meetings and following up on joint agreements.

The position will involve limited travel. It is primarily research-oriented. Teaching and supervision duties may be included, depending also on the candidate’s interests and preferences.

Expectations of qualifications

The applicant who is hired must have a Ph.D. degree in epidemiology, health sciences, biostatistics or data science with a strong focus on health. Candidates who have not yet completed their Ph.D. may apply if they expect to obtain the degree by the starting date. However, we envisage that, in addition to their Ph.D., the candidate will have at least 1–2 years of research-related experience, for example as a postdoc, research assistant or statistician.

The applicant must have the following qualifications:

• 
A clear academic interest in research on women’s mental health, including the relationships between reproductive life stages and mental disorders.

• 
First authorship of several scientific papers, including documented experience in epidemiological research based on register or cohort data.

• 
Documented experience with advanced epidemiological and statistical methods.

• 
Documented experience and competence in statistical programming, for example in R or Stata.

• 
A documented ability to independently plan studies, prepare study protocols, conduct analyses and write scientific papers.

• 
Good collaboration skills and the ability to take responsibility for tasks and contribute constructively to joint research projects.

• 
The ability to work systematically with data quality, documentation and the maintenance of research data.

• 
Fluency in written and spoken English.

The following would be an advantage but are not requirements:

• 
Experience in psychiatric epidemiology.

• 
Experience in the development or validation of prediction models.

• 
Practical experience with target trial emulation.

• 
Experience in international research collaborations.

• 
Written and spoken Danish, as Danish is the working language of the research unit.

Research environment

The position is based in the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, a growing, dynamic and collaborative research environment at the Department of Clinical Research, University of Southern Denmark. Our research group brings together expertise in psychiatry, psychology, epidemiology and public health. We offer a friendly, inclusive and interdisciplinary working environment where early-career researchers are supported in developing their academic and professional skills. The unit leads several major research projects focusing on perinatal mental health, child and adolescent psychiatry, and early intervention and prevention.

Research strategy for OUH and the Department of Clinical Research

The joint research strategy for the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital sets the direction for our shared research efforts in the years ahead. Rooted in the vision –We conduct research together to shape the patient care of the future – it focuses in particular on: cross-disciplinary research – with people at the centre; strong research environments – as drivers of development; and the research journey – from idea to impact. Further information on the joint research strategy of the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital is available here.

Further information 

For further information please contact Professor Trine Munk-Olsen, e-mail: tmun@sdu.dk, phone: +45 24 46 62 97.

Application deadline

November 18, 2026, at 23.59 hrs. (CET).

Interviews

Interviews are expected to take place in early December 2026.

Salary and terms of employment

The applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

The position as Postdoc is placed within salary steps 4–8 of the Danish state salary scale, depending on seniority. In addition, a centrally agreed postdoc allowance is paid, and further qualification- and function-related allowances may be negotiated.

The work location will be at Hospitalsringen 90, 5260 Odense S.  

Application

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below.

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.

The application must include (as PDF files) (please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total):

• 
a motivation letter

• 
a detailed CV

• 
degree certificates (inclusive of Ph.D.-diploma)

• 
a complete and numbered list of publications

• 
3 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please note that a copy of each publication must be attached as a pdf file.

• 
It is permitted to merge copies of the selected publications into a single PDF file.

• 
a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

• 
a detailed description of research experience

• 
an explanation of other qualifications relevant to the position

For technical issues, please contact: hcm-support@sdu.dk

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application.  

Applications received after the deadline and/or incomplete applications will not be considered.

Assessment

Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. 

The International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. 

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: Chef
jobs.description:
Vi har travlt og søger Kok til at indgå i vores køkkenteam i Køge, Greve og Slagelse.

Du er uddannet kok, gerne med erfaring fra enten hotel, restauration eller catering.

Du vil får grundigt oplæring og vi sørger for, at du løbende får ledelsestræning, så du bliverendnu bedre til at drive og udvikle køkkenet.

Dine daglige opgaver er bl.a.:

• 
Samarbejde med køkkenpersonale

• 
Bestilling og modtagelse af varer

• 
Opfølgning og tilsyn med takeaway

• 
Opfølgning af gæsternes mad i restauranten.

Du er glad, og smilende i din tilgang til andre mennesker, gæster såvel som kollagaer, også når der er rigtigt travlt.

Dine arbejdstimer ligger indenfor 12-22 og bliver fordelt via vagtplan.

Det er et krav at du behersker engelsk. I køkkenet arbejder flere forskellige nationaliteter ogrestaurantpersonalet er fortrinsvis danskere.

Har du ikke hørt fra os indenfor 14 dage, er det fordi jobbet er blevet besat.

 

ChefWe are busy and are looking for a Chef to join our kitchen team in Køge, Greve andSlagelse.You are a trained chef, preferably with experience in the hotel, restaurant, or catering.You will receive thorough training and we will ensure you continuously receive management training, so you become even better at running and developing the kitchen.

Your daily tasks include:

• 
Cooperation with kitchen staff

• 
Ordering and receiving goods

• 
Follow-up and supervision of takeaway

• 
Follow-up of the guests' food in the restaurant

You are happy and smiling in your approach to other people, guests as well as colleagues,even when it is really busy.Your working hours are between 12-22 and are distributed with a shift schedule.It is a requirement that you master in English. Several different nationalities work in the kitchen and the restaurant staff are mainly Danes.If you have not heard from us within 14 days, it is because the job has been filled.
